newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-London stocks close at third successive peak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-London stocks close at third successive peak.

text.p: London stocks were star performers on Wednesday, closing at a record level for the third straight session while the rest of Europe made losses, hurt by a negative start on Wall Street.

On currency markets, the dollar weakened against the yen after a news report said Japan, the United States and Germany were planning to intervene to sell dollars for yen and persuaded nervous traders to cut dollar positions.

London was lifted by a wave of optimism over the new Labour government's decision to take interest rate policy out of the political arena. Fears also receded of another interest rate hike in the near future.

"It is hard to over-estimate the impact of the move to give the Bank of England independence," one senior dealer said. "It has given investors confidence in our monetary policy. People think inflation can now actually be kept under control."
London fell back towards the end of the session after soaring nearly one percent to 4,562.0 on the blue-chip FTSE index, bettering the previous intra-day record set on Tuesday.
But the market, buoyed by the new bullish mood, managed to power through to close at a record of 4537.5 points, eclipsing successive closing peaks set in the last two trading sessions.

The rest of Europe was not so fortunate. Frankfurt floor trade finished down by nearly 0.5 percent after a record close on Tuesday. After-hours trading on the IBIS index also fell, as did Paris, after New York's early losses.

London's cracking performance was driven by investors who took heart from finance minister Gordon Brown's decision to leave the timing and size of interest rate adjustments to the Bank of England, the central bank.
British governments in the past have been accused of manipulating interest rates in order to win the favour of voters instead of making monetary decisions in the long-term interests of the economy.

At the same time, fears abated of further near-term interest rate hikes after Tuesday's 25-basis point increase because weak industrial production and manufacturing output data highlighted the damage done by the strong pound on corporate Britain.

"These figures serve as a timely reminder that industry needs more rises in interest rates, and the further rise in the pound they could prompt, like a hole in the head," said Jonathan Loynes, U.K. economist at HSBC Markets.
In Frankfurt, floor trade ended down 16.30 points at 3,551.98, depressed by Wall Street and as the approach of Thursday's Ascension Day holiday sapped investor interest.
"Nobody wants to make a bet right now," said a Frankfurt dealer. "This is not a day for testing any records."

Paris pre-holiday trade, up 0.4 percent in the morning session, turned sour as investors took profits and because of uncertainty about election opinion polls in the next few days. The CAC-40 index finished down 0.33 percent.
"It's mainly people squaring up ahead of the long weekend," a dealer said.

In currencies, the dollar was badly hit by the intervention talk, weakening by 1.5 yen in afternoon trade. The news report, citing an international monetary source, said the so-called Group of Three was exploring the possibility of a joint effort to sell dollars for yen to prevent further yen weakness.
"There hasn't been that much activity today but talk of intervention was enough to encourage a wave of profit-taking," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economic adviser at Bank of America.

The report on intervention, carried by Japan's Kyodo news agency, was fuelled later after a Japanese Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said Japan could use its $220 billion worth of external reserves promptly if needed.

U.S. Treasury Undersecretary Lawrence Summers declined to comment on the Kyodo report but confirmed that Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin had cut short a trip to Mexico to catch up with regular Treasury business.

Elsewhere, sterling was virtually unchanged after Tuesday's exuberant jump in reaction to the interest rate hike. In late European trade, the pound stood at $1.6366 and 2.8181 marks versus $1.6372 and 2.8185 marks in late Europe yesterday.
STOCKS PRICES
London's FTSE 100 finished up 18.2 points at 4,537.5.
The Paris CAC-40 index ended down 8.62 points at 2,643.31.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed down 16.30 points at 3,551.98.
CURRENCIES
The dollar stood at 1.7210 marks compared with 1.7229 marks late in Europe on Tuesday. It was at 124.93 yen, compared with 126.44.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $340.85 an ounce, compared with Tuesday's close in London of $342.85. Silver was $4.74, down one cent.
